newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine clitoris novel clinches record U.S. deal.
newsitem.headline: Argentine clitoris novel clinches record U.S. deal.

text.p: A controversial Argentine novel about an Italian scientist who claimed to have discovered the clitoris has been snapped up by a U.S. publisher, the book's local publishers said on Wednesday.
Doubleday will pay $200,000 for "The Anatomist," a first novel by young Argentine writer Federico Andahazi, said Guillermo Schavelzon, director of publishers, Editorial Planeta.
Doubleday confirmed the deal on Wednesday but declined comment on what it paid for the novel.
"The Anatomist" describes the life of a 16th century Italian scientist who discovered the clitoris when examining corpses and then studied its functions in bed with a Venetian prostitute.
The novel caused an Argentine literary scandal last year, when it was awarded the Fortabat Foundation prize, sponsored by wealthy businesswoman Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat.
Shocked by the book's subject, Fortabat rejected the competition jury's decision and refused to hand over the trophy, although she grudgingly gave Andahazi the advertised cash prize.
"This book does not defend Western, Christian values," Fortabat said at the time.
Planeta has since received many proposals to translate "Tha Anatomist," headed by the deal with Doubleday.
"Without doubt this is the highest sum paid up to now to publish a first novel by an Argentine writer in the United States," Schavelzon said.
